items.title: 54271_Charlie Holmes oral history interview
items.q: And then, when it come down to the band, then you had the band with Cootie plus Eddie Vinson.

ctx.x: I don't know. We came into the Savoy, and... No, we had been out with the Ink Spots. We had worked, oh, six months or more with the Ink Spots, and Ella Fitzgerald... We had a big show. Had a big show. It was quite a show. We played 27 theatres from New York to California. We played 27 theatres, and broke records at 26 theatres.. Broke records. I mean, in Chicago... There was a blizzard in Chicago, and there was a line around the corner of the Regal Theatre in Chicago, and that's a big theatre... And there was a…

items.title: 54271_Charlie Holmes oral history interview
items.q: when I was back with the Ink Spots, we had a show with the Ink Spots, Ella Fitzgerald, the Cootie Williams Band and Eddie 'Cleanhead' Vinson

ctx.x: No. Funny theatre. According to who... You know, one of them things. I played in there with Louis, and he packed the joint many a time. Packed, they'd be standing around the corner, trying to...waiting to get in. And other times I played there with him,...sometimes you could throw a baseball out in the audience, and you wouldn't hit nobody. It's just one of them things.

Maybe the week that you go in there is bad. Like the week before Easter, that's a very bad week in the theatre. Don't ask me why, but it is. I guess that's more or less Holy Week or something. It's bad. They have their good weeks and their bad weeks. They know exactly what's supposed to happen.
